Autódromo do Estoril — survey

Portugal · Portuguese GP (retired, classic) · theme green, day-only (night:false) · branch cursor/estoril-survey-a1 · base sha a830377 (shot-tooling + day-wet-lighting PR #1979 merged) · surveyed 2026-10-15 · read-only

72 frames: TLX renderer, SwiftShader, 960 px wide, seen here at 800 px. Measured facts come from the built centreline (buildCenterline) and audit-circuit; source claims are labelled; guesses are labelled hypothesis.

Summary

  • Layout builds cleanly: verify-track OK, 0 surface folds, 0 floating, 0 buried; clip audit 2 severe = baseline 2.
  • The biggest visible problems are shared lighting/reflection issues in wet weather (D1) and sky response in overcast/fog (D5), then Estoril-specific vegetation and material look (D2–D4).
  • Landmarks in the brief exist in code and are required modelGroups; the moinho is flagged uncertain by the author.

Gallery

Day · dry — orbit (6 lap positions)

Baseline. Parasol pines read correctly, but the generic stacked-cone firs and yellow tiered trees sit next to them, the horizon is a ring of flat-topped blocks, and the f33 church reads as grey gridded masonry rather than limewash (defects D2, D3, D4).

Day · dry — eye (driver view)

Straight-on views. Frame 07 shows the pit complex on the right as a dark slab; frames 10–12 show firs among the pines. Racing-line arrows are the player assist, not a defect.

Day · dry — trackside

Camera framing issues: 13 is blocked by a building wall, 15 has a riveted panel at the right edge (camera tower or marshal post), 16 has a terrain wedge in the foreground (D8).

Day · wet

Surface darkens and the sky goes dull purple-grey. Prop reflections appear as ghost copies below the trees (D1).

Day · rain

As wet, plus rain streaks. Planar-reflection ghosts and dithered vertical streaks under the tree line at f33 (D1).

Day · overcast

Ground and fog respond but the sky stays saturated blue — overcast does not desaturate or grey the dome (D5).

Day · fog

Patchy blotchy fog on the ground; zenith stays vivid blue; the far ridge ring fades into haze (D5).

Day · storm

Sky does grey out and the scene is dark, but the ground is an almost black mirror. Reflection artefacts are strongest here (D1). Storm at day looks like dusk rather than daytime storm light; the PR #1979 change is in this tree.

Dusk · dry

Warm amber ground pools along the whole lap although the def sets lamp:"none" (see U3). Sky goes deep blue; fog and props fade plausibly.

Dusk · rain

Wet reflections of lit pools; ghost props again.

Night · dry

Dark sky, lit pools on tarmac and gravel, lit stands at f00 and f83. Not a night:true circuit, so no authored night scenery.

Night · rain

Strong wet specular on the pit apron; church base reflects cleanly in f33, ghost trees at f17/f50.

Ranked defects

D1 — Wet / rain / storm: planar-reflection ghosts and dithered streaks [High (visual)]
Frames 20–30, 43–48, 55–60, 67–72. Trees and the church are mirrored on the ground as smeared copies; at f33 storm a comb of vertical dark streaks sits under the tree line. Not Estoril-specific — expect it on every circuit. Not in the circuit files: the reflection pass in the wet-surface shader / js/lighting/atmosphere.js (just changed by PR #1979). Suggested fix: fade or clip the mirror pass by roughness and prop height, or cap reflection tap count. Mechanism not traced.
D2 — Limewash and terracotta not visible: church, aldeia, pit terrace and timing tower read grey [Medium]
The aldeia church (frame 03) is a grey gridded block with an orange roof, not limewash. The pit terrace (frame 01, left) is a flat grey-beige slab, no azulejo band or pantile read. These groups stage with stage._mat = MAT.CONCRETE (scenery/estoril.js:75, 108, 291, 301, 328, 337) over LIME [0.95,0.94,0.90]; AGENTS.md says the baked pack is blended as albedo × tex.rgb × 2.0, so a grey concrete layer would pull the limewash grey (hypothesis from reading, not measured). Suggested fix: use MAT.PLASTER or mat 0 for walls if one exists, or lift LIME; check with __apex.matTex(0) A/B.
D3 — Generic stacked-cone firs and tiered yellow trees contradict the brief [Medium]
Brief §6: the stacked-cone conifer draws a northern fir. Frames 02, 10–12, 15 show many. Cause: forestEdge(..., pineFrac: 0.82) at scenery/estoril.js:380 (two ranges × two sides) plus the tree() cork-oak at :55 which comes out as a yellow tiered shape with the broad/vase furniture (def :85). Small cone bushes (:48) read as stray green pyramids on the verge. Suggested fix: set pineFrac to 0 or route forestEdge through stonePine (:21) / acacia (:387); recolour the yellow.
D4 — Horizon: ring of flat-topped grey blocks; Serra de Sintra not visible [Medium]
Every day frame shows the skyline as a row of boxy slabs from the hill ring (scenery/estoril.js:248–260, three rings 42/32/24 ridges, len 130–240 m, hMin 14–48 m). The three Serra mountains (:269–278, 5.1–5.6 km, 224–348 m) are not distinguishable in any frame. Guess: exponential fog at density 0.003 (def :39) leaves almost nothing at 5 km (exp(−0.003×5090)≈2e-7), or the camera far plane clips them. Suggested fix: rounder ridge profile; reduce or exclude the Serra from fog, or raise their tint toward horizon colour.
D5 — Overcast and fog keep a saturated blue sky [Medium]
Frames 31–42: ground goes grey-green and hazy but the dome stays the clear-day gradient. Fog ground blotches look patchy (low-res noise). Engine/lighting, not circuit data (js/lighting/atmosphere.js, weather-arc.js); report to the lighting owner.
D6 — Broadcast compound suppressed; 13 trees dropped [Low]
verify-track: guard drops broadcastCompound=1 tree=13. The compound at scenery/estoril.js:131 (K(0.918), 68 m) and 13 trees do not emit. Likely the preflight footprint rejecting against T13/T14 gravel+stand clutter. Either relocate the compound or remove the call.
D7 — Turn table has 14 entries; brief and docs say 13 corners; built length 4.138 km vs 4.182 official [Low]
def.turns (js/circuits/estoril.js:84) lists T14 as the Parabólica after the Esses; docs/tracks/estoril.md says 13 corners. Built total 4137.97 m (def comment says 4.140; path.len 4171; official 4182 m, −1.1 %). Doc drift more than defect; update the brief or the numbering.
D8 — Trackside camera frames blocked by props or terrain [Low (tooling)]
Frames 13, 15 and 16: building wall, tower panel, terrain wedge. shot.mjs is meant to step round obstructions, so it did not for these; seat of cameraTower (:399, f0.43) and marshalPost placements in the trackside lane could be checked.
D9 — Pit terrace and stands at f00: large featureless flat grey area [Low]
Frame 01, left half of image: a very large untextured grey plane beside the straight with one hard black edge line. Probably the pit lane / paddock apron (engine, not estoril.js) or the terrace roof deck (scenery:85, LIME_D). Not resolved.

Not captured / uncertain

  • U1. Matrix cut: no eye/trackside for weather, dusk or night (orbit only); no dawn; no aerial grid; no capture of the deposito, moinho or Serra on purpose-framed shots (all >100 m off the lap, not in any frame).
  • U2. Terrain-over-road and sunk water: not judged beyond what the frames show (none seen); the audit counts are the evidence.
  • U3. Dusk/night amber pools with lamp:"none": source of the light not traced (could be the engine's generic lamps or car lights).
  • U4. Banking built values, brief-vs-real corner count and the moinho's reality were not checked against external sources this pass.
  • U5. Frame-to-defect file:line links for D1 and D5 point to a module, not a line: the mechanism was not traced.
